title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of TPG Telecom. Confined to the Window Periods, need written acknowledgement from the Chairperson to trade outside them (the Chairperson needs it from the Chairperson of the Audit Committee), must give written confirmation to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion, must advise all trading by them or entities they control, and must disclose Security Arrangements to the designated officer.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Any person engaged in the management of TPG Telecom, whether as an employee or consultant, including the Chief Executive Officer and at least the top two levels of management below the CEO. Subject to the same Window Periods, with written acknowledgement from the CEO for out-of-window trades and written confirmation within 5 business days of completion.

tiers.name: employees and consultants
tiers.description: Employees and consultants of TPG Telecom who are not Directors or Senior Executives. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and expressly permitted to take out margin loans over vested holdings, but not subject to the Window Period, written acknowledgement, short-term trading or Security Arrangement disclosure provisions, which are addressed only to Directors and Senior Executives.

tiers.name: persons or entities controlled by them
tiers.description: Entities or trusts controlled by a person or in which the person has an interest, to which the insider trading prohibition extends; Directors must also advise TPG Telecom of trading in Securities by persons or entities controlled by them.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairperson of the Board may impose an ad hoc closed period prohibiting Directors and Senior Executives from trading at times while TPG Telecom is considering a matter subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A. The Policy does not say whether the existence or reason for such a closed period is confidential.

rules.detail: No derivatives rule. Securities are defined to include derivatives, so entering into a put or call over TPG Telecom shares is dealing in Securities. Inside a Window Period no acknowledgement is required, but the Director must still advise the Company Secretary in writing within 2 business days for onward ASX notification within 5 business days; outside a Window Period the Director needs written acknowledgement from the Chairperson and must identify Exceptional Circumstances on the annexed form.
rules.evidence: Securities include shares of any class, options, bonds, derivatives, managed investments and superannuation products and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Same treatment as Directors: derivatives over TPG Telecom Securities are Securities, dealing is confined to the Window Periods, and out-of-window dealing requires written acknowledgement from the Chief Executive Officer, with written confirmation of the completed trade to the Company Secretary within 5 business days.
rules.evidence: a Senior Executive of TPG Telecom must inform and obtain written acknowledgement from the Chief Executive Officer prior to undertaking the trade

rules.detail: The Window Period, written acknowledgement and short-term trading provisions are all addressed to Directors and Senior Executives only. For other employees and consultants the Policy imposes nothing beyond the insider trading prohibition.

The Policy contains no hedging provision. There is no definition of hedging or of limiting economic risk, and no restriction on hedging unvested or holding-locked incentive securities; any such restriction would have to come from the equity plan rules, which are not incorporated.

Monetisation and prepaid forwards are not named. Such a structure is a derivative and therefore a Security, so it is confined to the Window Periods or requires written acknowledgement, and if it encumbers the Director's Securities it is a Security Arrangement whose details must be given to the designated officer on entry and on any non-trivial change.
rules.evidence: any Director or Senior Executive of TPG Telecom who enters into margin lending arrangements or otherwise encumbers their Securities of TPG Telecom (“Security Arrangements”) is required to provide details of those Security Arrangements to the relevant “designated officer”

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and there is no economic-effect test that would capture a downside position.
Securities lending is not mentioned. The Security Arrangements provision covers margin lending and encumbrances, not stock loans, and there is no dealing definition that would sweep a stock loan in.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives and therefore Securities, so the Window Period and written acknowledgement regime applies. A CFD closed within three months would also offend the prohibition on dealing for short term gain.
rules.evidence: Directors and Senior Executives must not deal in TPG Telecom's Securities for short term gain. Short term means a period of three months or less.

rules.detail: Margin loans over vested holdings are expressly permitted, subject to disclosure of the Security Arrangements to the designated officer on entry and on any non-trivial change, including the number of Securities, any trigger points and the lender's right to sell unilaterally. The permission extends equally to Senior Executives, employees and consultants. The one substantive limit is that a margin call must not be met by a sale at a time when the person could not sell under the Policy.
rules.evidence: Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants of TPG Telecom may take out margin loans over their vested holdings in TPG Telecom's Securities.

rules.detail: The express permission is confined to vested holdings. The Policy does not say what happens to unvested holdings used as collateral, so there is no express prohibition but no express permission either.

Identical to Directors: permitted over vested holdings, with details of the Security Arrangements to be given to the Chief Executive Officer as designated officer on entry and on any non-trivial change, and no margin call to be met by a sale at a prohibited time.

rules.detail: Encumbering TPG Telecom Securities is expressly contemplated and is not prohibited; it triggers the Security Arrangements disclosure obligation to the designated officer on entry and on any change other than a trivial or minor one, so the Company can meet its ASX Listing Rule 3.1 obligations. The Policy warns that Security Arrangements may still be subject to the dealing prohibitions in the Policy.

rules.detail: Secured financing over vested TPG Telecom Securities is permitted rather than prohibited. There is no approval requirement for the financing itself, only disclosure to the designated officer, and no size threshold, LVR limit or minimum retained holding.

rules.detail: Directors and Senior Executives must not deal for short term gain, short term being defined as three months or less. There are no carve-outs, although plan acquisitions, dividend reinvestment, share purchase plans and conversions are excluded from the Policy altogether.

exemption_authority: The relevant designated officer (the Chairperson for Directors, the Chairperson of the Audit Committee for the Chairperson, the Chief Executive Officer for Senior Executives) may give written acknowledgement permitting a trade outside a Window Period, typically in Exceptional Circumstances. The acknowledgement is expressly a compliance monitoring function only and not an endorsement of the transaction, and the individual remains responsible for compliance with the law.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants of TPG Telecom may take out margin loans over their vested holdings in TPG Telecom's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted rather than banned, provided it is secured only over vested holdings; this is one of the few ASX policies that affirmatively allows a director to encumber shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: However, Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants must not allow a margin call to be met by the sale of TPG Telecom's Securities at a time when they would not be able to sell those Securities themselves under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement and physical settlement rights must be drafted so that no sale of the collared shares can occur outside a Window Period or during an ad hoc closed period without the executive first obtaining written acknowledgement, otherwise the executive breaches the Policy through the lender's own action.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The details of the Security Arrangements which must be provided must include the number of Securities of TPG Telecom involved, any trigger points, the right of the lender or security holder to sell the Securities unilaterally and any other material details.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Commercial terms of the facility, including margin triggers and the bank's unilateral sale rights, must be handed to the Chairperson or CEO at inception and on every non-trivial amendment, and may be announced to the market under Listing Rule 3.1.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written acknowledgement is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction. Individuals remain responsible for their compliance with the law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot treat the designated officer's acknowledgement as company sign-off on the collar's legality, so it should obtain its own confirmation on insider information and plan-rule compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Senior Executives are only permitted to deal in TPG Telecom's Securities during a one month period following the release of TPG Telecom's half yearly and annual results ... and TPG Telecom's Annual General Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a closed-by-default policy with only three one-month windows a year, so collar entry, roll and unwind must be scheduled into those windows or justified as Exceptional Circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Outside the Window Period, Directors and Senior Executives may in certain circumstances (for example, Exceptional Circumstances) trade in TPG Telecom's Securities following written acknowledgement in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The annexed form requires details of the Exceptional Circumstances, so a voluntary financing transaction is unlikely to be executable outside a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include shares of any class, options, bonds, derivatives, managed investments and superannuation products and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Derivatives are listed expressly, but the closing words 'able to be traded on a financial market' could be argued to confine the definition to exchange-traded products, leaving it unclear whether a bilateral OTC put and call are Securities for Policy purposes; confirm the company's view before relying on either reading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Senior Executives must not deal in TPG Telecom's Securities for short term gain. Short term means a period of three months or less.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind should exceed three months, and the structure should not be characterised as dealing for short term gain.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no hedging prohibition, no restriction on hedging unvested or holding-locked equity, and no short-selling prohibition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is prohibited by the trading policy itself; the constraints on hedging unvested incentive securities would have to come from the plan rules and section 206J of the Corporations Act, which are outside this document.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it may lead to disciplinary action being taken against the person, including disposal of any TPG Telecom Securities acquired in breach of this Policy and/or dismissal in serious cases.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach can trigger forced disposal of the underlying shares, which would cut across a collar and the bank's security position.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at TPG Telecom, which is among the most permissive ASX policies on financing. The Policy expressly allows Directors, Senior Executives, employees and consultants to take out margin loans over their vested holdings and contemplates that they may 'otherwise encumber' their Securities, subject only to disclosure of the Security Arrangements to the designated officer (the Chairperson for Directors, the CEO for Senior Executives) on entry and on any non-trivial change, including the number of shares, trigger points and the lender's unilateral sale rights, which may in turn be disclosed to ASX under Listing Rule 3.1. There is no hedging, short-selling or derivatives prohibition, and derivatives fall within the definition of Securities, so both option legs are ordinary dealings that must be executed inside one of the three one-month Window Periods following the half year results, the annual results and the AGM, or outside them with written acknowledgement supported by Exceptional Circumstances. The critical structuring constraint is that a margin call must not be met by a sale of TPG Telecom Securities at a time when the executive could not sell, so the bank's enforcement and physical-settlement rights must be conditioned on Policy-permitted timing. Collateral should be limited to vested holdings and the tenor should exceed three months to stay clear of the short-term gain prohibition.
